beats.hook: I gave a eulogy at my best friend's funeral. Three days later, I found out he was alive.
beats.setup: Marcus and I had been best friends since college. When I got the call that he'd died in a car accident — I didn't question it.
beats.incident: His "sister" reached out. Said the family wanted me to speak. I'd never met her before, but Marcus always said they were close. I stood at that podium and cried in front of two hundred strangers. That part still haunts me — because I don't think any of them actually knew him.
beats.escalation: A week later, a mutual friend sent me a photo. Marcus. Alive. Standing at an airport in another country. Turns out he owed money — a lot of it — to people who don't send collection notices. He faked his death. And he needed someone credible to make the funeral feel real. He chose me.
beats.payoff: I was the alibi. The grieving best friend who made everyone believe it. The "sister" was hired. The whole thing was staged — and I was the only one in that room who didn't know. The moment I understood that, something went quiet in me. Like a door closing.
beats.cta: I've never spoken to him again. But here's what I still can't answer — if he reached out tomorrow, would I turn him in? What would you do?
